paragraphs.text: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by hamartomatous polyps of the gastrointestinal tract and mucocutaneous melanin deposits (Giardiello et al., 1987). The melanin spots occur on the lips, buccal mucosa, and digits (Hemminki et al., 1997). Patients have an increased risk for various neoplasms, including gastrointestinal cancer (Jenne et al., 1998). Gastrointestinal tumors and cancers of the breast, ovary, testis, and uterine cervix appear to be overrepresented (Hemminki et al., 1997). Mehenni et al. (1997) described the disorder as having variable expression and incomplete penetrance, and Mehenni et al. (1998) noted that the increased risk of benign and malignant tumors applies both to the gastrointestinal tract and to tissues outside it. Hemminki et al. (1998) described PJS as a rare hereditary disease that predisposes to benign and malignant tumors in many organ systems.
